title: India Rejects Pakistan's 'State-Sponsored Disinformation' at ASEAN Forum in Manila
excerpt: MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal accused Pakistan of exploiting the ASEAN Regional Forum to spread falsehoods, while reaffirming that the Indus Waters Treaty remains in abeyance until Islamabad ends support for cross-border terrorism.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • India condemned Pakistan's claims at ASEAN as baseless and disinformation.
  • Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh are integral parts of India, according to MEA.
  • The Indus Waters Treaty is suspended until Pakistan stops supporting terrorism.
  • India is prioritizing five hydropower projects totaling over 4,800 MW in the Chenab basin.

India on Thursday delivered a sharp rebuke to Pakistan after Islamabad raised the Kashmir dispute and criticised the suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty at the ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) in Manila. Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Pakistan had "cynically exploited" the multilateral platform to amplify falsehoods and deflect attention from its own record of sponsoring cross-border terrorism.

"It is no surprise that a multilateral forum has once again been cynically exploited by Pakistan to amplify falsehoods, peddle state-sponsored disinformation, and divert attention from its own well-documented record of sponsoring cross-border terrorism."

— Randhir Jaiswal, MEA Spokesperson

India's Position on Kashmir and the Treaty

Jaiswal stated categorically that "the Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh have been, are and will always remain integral and inalienable parts of India," adding that Pakistan has "no locus standi to comment on the same."

On the Indus Waters Treaty, Jaiswal said India's position remains consistent: the 1960 pact stands in abeyance following Pakistan's continued sponsorship of terrorism, including the April 2025 Pahalgam attack that killed 26 people. "IWT will continue to be held in abeyance until Pakistan credibly and irrevocably abjures its support for cross-border terrorism," he said.

The abeyance, stemming from a Cabinet Committee on Security decision on April 23, 2025, has left all institutional mechanisms under the treaty inoperative — including Permanent Indus Commission meetings, inspections, and the routine exchange of hydrological data. India has, however, continued to issue flood warnings on humanitarian grounds, voluntarily providing 23 warnings during the last flood season outside the treaty framework.

![Randhir Jaiswal. Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Pakistan had "cynically exploited" the multilateral platform to amplify falsehoods and deflect attention from its own record of sponsoring cross-border terrorism.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/0c/H20260611210655.jpg)

Hydropower Push and Strategic Calculus

With the treaty frozen, India has outlined an accelerated push for hydropower development in the Chenab basin. Five major projects — the 1,856 MW Sawalkote, 1,000 MW Pakal Dul, 850 MW Ratle, 624 MW Kiru, and 540 MW Kwar — have been identified as priorities, according to government sources cited by The Hindu Business Line.

India has argued that the treaty, negotiated based on 1950s engineering, no longer reflects present-day realities. "India's population demographics, need to generate clean energy, water demand for irrigation and drinking water, climate change challenges and technological capabilities have changed fundamentally," sources told ANI. India had asked Pakistan to reassess the treaty's provisions in 2023, but Islamabad declined.

Pakistan's delegation at the ARF was led by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar, who raised the Kashmir dispute and called for its resolution per UN Security Council resolutions. Dar also expressed concern over India's decision to hold the treaty in abeyance.

Jaiswal also took aim at what he described as Pakistan's practice of propagating "officially sponsored disinformation, often dressed in religious terminology such as the use of terms like 'Fitna al-Hindustan.'" He called it "a futile attempt by the Pakistani establishment to deflect attention from its own internal crises."

"Pakistan would serve itself better by dismantling the infrastructure of terrorism on its soil and putting its own house in order instead of pointing fingers at its neighbours."

— Randhir Jaiswal, MEA Spokesperson

Wider ASEAN Engagements

External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar attended the ARF and related foreign minister-level meetings in Manila over July 22-23, holding bilateral talks with counterparts from Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and the United States. On the sidelines, Jaishankar also participated in the Quad Foreign Ministers' Meeting with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and his Australian and Japanese counterparts, with discussions covering trade, tariffs, defence, critical minerals, and AI.

The exchange underscores the broader freeze in India-Pakistan relations since Operation Sindoor in May 2025 and the continued weaponisation of multilateral forums by both sides. India has maintained that "terrorism and talks cannot go together," a position that shows no sign of softening despite periodic international calls for dialogue.
